tags.name: Universal
tags.description: Literal item or service fits essentially any broad setting without requiring a modern, futuristic, or magical reinterpretation.

tags.name: Fantasy
tags.description: Content appropriate to a fantasy campaign, including the ordinary medieval-style weapons, armor, clothing, services, and tools that such a setting needs as well as explicitly magical content.

tags.name: Historical
tags.description: Period-specific mundane content from ancient, medieval, early-modern, or other historical settings. This is broad historical coverage, not a medieval-only filter.

tags.name: Modern
tags.description: Industrial, contemporary, electronic, or institutionally modern content.

tags.name: Horror
tags.description: Content specifically tied to occult, supernatural, macabre, or horror themes. Combine it with the campaign's normal era or genre tag.

tags.name: Post-Apocalyptic
tags.description: Content specifically tied to collapse, scavenging, improvised survival, radiation, or post-collapse conditions. Ordinary modern objects come from Modern instead.

tags.name: Sci-Fi
tags.description: Futuristic, advanced, spacefaring, or speculative technology. Combine with Modern when the setting also retains ordinary contemporary technology.

tags.name: Black Market
tags.description: Illicit, restricted, contraband, or underground-market goods and services. This is a purchasing overlay rather than an era.

rules.ruleText: Mk3 begins with complete representative base items that establish each item family’s ordinary pattern.
rules.implementationGuidance: The base is an authoring example only. Future variants are complete standalone records in the same Family.

rules.ruleText: A future variant belongs to the same Family as its base pattern but stores all of its own final values.
rules.implementationGuidance: When creating a variant, copy the base as a starting point, make the changes, and save a complete independent record.

rules.ruleName: When to Create a New Family
rules.ruleText: Keep an item in an existing Family when it is fundamentally the same kind of object with a different material, configuration, quality, technology, or similar variation. Create a new Family when its core operation substantially differs.
rules.implementationGuidance: Longsword and Titanium Longsword can share Longsword. Longsword and Rapier are different Families. An M16-style rifle can share the 5.56 mm Rifle Family.

rules.ruleText: Catalog scope controls where the G.O.D. authors and manages an Item definition. Equipment contains weapons, armor, and general gear intended to be worn, wielded, carried, or actively used as equipment. Inventory contains all other catalog definitions, including ammunition, consumables, materials, services, property, vehicles, companions, and ordinary possessions. Catalog scope does not determine every mechanic an Item may possess.
rules.implementationGuidance: Use Window/Catalog Scope only to choose the Heavens Equipment or Inventory authoring window. Do not infer player ownership or equipped state. Optional profiles extend the Item independently of scope; for example, an Inventory Ammunition definition still has a Weapon/Ammunition profile.

rules.ruleText: Items do not store character Skill requirements or Skill links.
rules.implementationGuidance: The character/rules system determines how an item is used. Magic interaction is handled by the magic system, not an item Skill column.

rules.ruleText: Melee and thrown weapons deal their own listed damage. Firearms, bows, crossbows, launchers, and similar ammunition-fed weapons use ammunition as their damage source.
rules.implementationGuidance: The launcher only changes ammunition output when an explicit weapon rule says so.

rules.ruleText: Base ammunition is stored on the Weapons tab alongside weapons. Special ammunition is added later as a complete standalone record in the appropriate ammunition Family.
rules.implementationGuidance: Use the base ammunition as the authoring pattern, then save the special ammunition with all of its own final values.

rules.ruleText: Armor Base Soak is flat damage reduction at a covered Body Shot Bob location.
rules.implementationGuidance: Damage modifiers adjust Base Soak by damage type. Worn layers resolve sequentially.

rules.ruleText: Durability is actual item HP. Damage absorbed by armor reduces that armor layer’s durability by the amount absorbed.
rules.implementationGuidance: At 0 durability an item is broken or unusable until repaired or replaced.

rules.ruleText: Credits are the universal underlying value for catalog entries.
rules.implementationGuidance: Campaign-specific currencies convert to or from Credits. Price_Basis states what quantity, duration, service, or unit the listed Credits buy.

rules.ruleText: Tags are bulk campaign-selection filters. Universal is deliberately strict and only covers literal items that fit essentially any broad setting.
rules.implementationGuidance: Combine packs rather than making one tag do everything. Examples: medieval fantasy = Universal + Fantasy; broad historical = Universal + Historical; contemporary horror = Universal + Modern + Horror; post-apocalyptic = Universal + Modern + Post-Apocalyptic; spacefaring sci-fi may use Universal + Modern + Sci-Fi.

rules.ruleText: Properties stores only simple supporting facts that do not deserve a specialized table.
rules.implementationGuidance: Use it for capacities, charges, passengers, cargo, propulsion, creature links, sale units, and similar basic facts.

rules.ruleText: Purchasable companions or animals may be Catalog entries that link to the Creature system.
rules.implementationGuidance: Creature statistics remain in the Creature system; the Item catalog never duplicates them.

rules.ruleText: Training, enchantments, installed attachments, conditions, and similar modifiers are not part of the base seed unless they are independently purchasable objects.
rules.implementationGuidance: Those systems are implemented later in the working program. If they produce a sellable item variant, that item is saved as a complete record in the appropriate Family.

rules.ruleText: Mk3 is the canonical starting catalog of complete base-pattern items and essential mechanics, not the full item editor.
rules.implementationGuidance: Future family variants, enchantments, attachments, training, and other editor behavior are created in the program as complete records when that system is built.

rules.ruleText: Currency and exchange items may leave Credits blank when their value depends on the campaign exchange rate.
rules.implementationGuidance: Use Price_Basis = campaign exchange rate rather than inventing a universal fixed conversion.
